close_reason:
Moved the MDN/parse blob-id cap onto MdnBackend as fn max_mdn_parse_blob_ids(caller, account_id) -> usize with default MDN_PARSE_MAX_BLOB_IDS (16). The handler reads the cap at request time, eliminating the const-vs-handler-arg duplication and giving backends per-account flexibility. Matches the existing MailBackend per-method max_<thing>(caller, account_id) convention; the workspace AGENTS.md 'Backend caps and limits' section blesses this pre-existing shape for jmap-mail-server.

API impact (pre-1.0 break, internal callers only):
- handle_mdn_parse: drops the max_blob_ids parameter
- register_mdn_handlers: drops the max_blob_ids parameter
- MDN_PARSE_MAX_BLOB_IDS const: kept, retconned to 'this is the trait method's default value' rather than 'pass this to the handler' — backward-compat for external consumers that already use the const by name

Quality gates: fmt + clippy --all-features --tests + test --all-features + doc --all-features all clean. New integration test pins default-16 cap against 17-blob-IDs requestTooLarge response.

Did NOT pursue the bead's Option 2 (Option<usize> with None=use-const) — the trait-method approach is the workspace-canonical shape for this kind of cap and is more flexible (per-account). Did NOT touch sibling extension-server crates because no sibling currently has an analogous MDN-or-parse-style blob-count cap; this is mail-server-local.

Cookie-cutter posture: the trait-method pattern is the workspace-canonical shape, so future sibling extension-server caps (e.g. a hypothetical SearchSnippet/get blob-id cap, a hypothetical Sieve script-import batch cap) should be added via the same fn max_<thing>(caller, account_id) shape — NOT via const+handler-arg. No separate propagation bead needed because no sibling currently has the bug.
description:
src/mdn.rs:537 declares:

```
pub const MDN_PARSE_MAX_BLOB_IDS: usize = 16;
```

src/mdn.rs:547 (handle_mdn_parse) takes a runtime parameter:

```
pub async fn handle_mdn_parse<B: MailBackend + MdnBackend>(
    backend: &B,
    caller: &B::CallerCtx,
    args: Value,
    max_blob_ids: usize,
) -> ...
```

src/lib.rs:278 (register_mdn_handlers) takes the limit at registration time:

```
pub fn register_mdn_handlers<B>(
    dispatcher: &mut Dispatcher<B::CallerCtx>,
    backend: Arc<B>,
    max_blob_ids: usize,
)
```

The default value (16) is encoded in the `pub const`, NOT in the registration function or the handler signature. A consumer who wants the default writes:

```
register_mdn_handlers(&mut dispatcher, backend, jmap_mail_server::mdn::MDN_PARSE_MAX_BLOB_IDS);
```

…which is a verbose ceremony. The doc explicitly tells callers to do this (lib.rs:269: "Pass [`mdn::MDN_PARSE_MAX_BLOB_IDS`] for the default").

Contract issues:

1. **Changing the default is a multi-site edit.** A future tightening from 16 to 8 means changing the const AND auditing every caller (kith, stoa, third parties) to confirm they pass the const rather than a hardcoded literal. The const is not authoritative; the registered-handler-time value is.

2. **No way to NOT cap.** If a high-volume deployment wants no cap, the caller passes `usize::MAX` — which works but the doc does not document this idiom. `Option<usize>` with `None = no cap` would be clearer.

3. **The cap is enforced at the handler, not at the backend.** A caller wanting per-account variation cannot — `register_mdn_handlers` takes one value for all accounts. Compare with `max_collapse_threads_emails(caller, account_id) -> usize` on `MailBackend`, which is per-account.

Defensive shape:
- Move the cap onto `MdnBackend` as `fn max_mdn_parse_blob_ids(caller, account_id) -> usize { 16 }` to match the rest of the workspace cap convention.
- OR change the signature to `Option<usize>` with `None` meaning "use the constant".

Priority P2 because: not a correctness bug, the current shape works, but the duplicated default and per-account inflexibility lock the maintainer in if a 1.0 contract is shipped before this gets revisited.
title: MDN_PARSE_MAX_BLOB_IDS default duplicated across const and handler parameter
